issue: Does Supreme Court precedent (Chambers v. Mississippi) require courts to assess cumulative prejudice when reviewing a state conviction under the Due Process Clause?
provision: U.S. Const. amend. XIV (Due Process Clause); 28 U.S.C. § 2254(d)(1)

sides.position: Supreme Court precedent mandates cumulative prejudice analysis in the due process context.
Cumulative prejudice analysis is not required by Supreme Court due process precedent.

quote: Other circuits disagree. See Williams v. Anderson, 460 F.3d 789, 817 (6th Cir. 2006).
cite: James Scott v. Ron Broomfield, No. 22-99000 (9th Cir. 2026)
